**Your impact begins here

**As Accounting Controller, you will keep month-end close accurate and on time across a number of countries in Business Area (BA)West, while making the way we work simpler. You will oversee key affiliate finance processes, support Accounting Managers and drive projects that standardise, simplify and digitalise accounting. Your work gives affiliates reliable financial information and the support they need, strengthening Finance across Novo.

**What You’ll Bring

**To succeed in this role, you bring:

• A master’s degree in business, finance, economics or a similar field.

• More than 4 years of relevant experience from finance, consulting or a related environment, including accounting, financial reporting or finance operations.

• A solid understanding of month-end close activities and core finance processes, with knowledge of Procure-to-Pay (P2P), Record-to-Report (R2R) and/or Order-to-Cash (O2C).

• SAP experience.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to carry out structured ad hoc analyses.

• Experience working with stakeholders across countries or business areas.

• A proactive, service-oriented mindset, with strong organisational and communication skills and attention to detail.

• The ability to manage routine activities while contributing to projects and improvement initiatives, and the confidence to raise questions and drive improvements.

**What You’ll Do

**You will combine reliable delivery of day-to-day accounting with active work to improve how accounting runs across Business Area West.

• Perform routine accounting and reporting tasks for a number of countries during month-end close.

• Oversee affiliate finance processes across P2P, R2R and O2C, monitor process performance and follow up on issues to keep delivery timely and accurate.

• Support Accounting Managers with ad hoc analyses, reporting and general accounting questions.

• Guide and support affiliates and relevant Finance stakeholders.

• Participate in and drive projects across Accounting and Finance, identifying opportunities to improve processes, efficiency and collaboration.

• Contribute to standardisation and continuous improvement across the Accounting & Taxation organisation.

You will join the Accounting & Taxation BA West Centre of Excellence (CoE), based in Copenhagen, and report to the Associate Director Accounting & Taxation CoE. The CoE is responsible for Accounting & Taxation for nine affiliates across 11 countries: Denmark & Iceland, Sweden, Norway, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium & Luxembourg, Finland, Ireland and Portugal. It provides expertise, governance and support across accounting, tax, compliance and process excellence.

The team includes Accounting Managers and controllers who work as dedicated finance partners to individual affiliates, while two roles focus on the Business Area as a whole. You will work closely with Accounting Managers, affiliates and Finance stakeholders, and with colleagues in our shared service centre in Bangalore. Together you will keep processes running reliably and speak up early when something needs follow-up.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will work in an international finance environment where your expertise is valued and your voice counts. Combining day-to-day accounting with improvement projects gives you room to build new skills, broaden your view of Finance across several countries and see the difference your ideas make.

You will be supported to perform at your best and trusted to take ownership, in a team that works together to improve how accounting runs.

• Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,180.00 to 838,130.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are motivated by delivering high-quality accounting support and making change happen across a complex organisation, apply by 19.11.2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.description:
Do you want to develop cutting-edge software applications for our world-leading products? Looking to use and grow your development skills in a fast-paced and creative environment? If this sounds like an exciting challenge, we’d love to hear from you!

Team Sport Application: Where Trackman goes beyond golf

Trackman products generate extremely accurate measurements using a patented combination of camera and radar, which provide valuable insights for athletes ranging from top worldclass professionals to enthusiastic amateurs, as well as coaches, scouts, analysts and clubs of all levels.

As part of our company's continued expansion, we are looking for a .NET C# backend developer. You will join a department of 45+ skilled developers, and work in our Team Sport Application department, responsible for products used in baseball, softball, American football and football (soccer). You will be part of refinement, planning, implementation, testing and deployment to our customers.

We build applications hosted on distributed Linux servers running Docker, on Microsoft Azure technologies, on mobile devices and customer laptops. You will get to interact with skilled developers working across a range of platforms and apps. We always work with the latest LTS .NET version using C# with web frontends in React.

As part of our development toolkit, our teams actively use AI-assisted tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude to speed up coding, testing, and documentation — letting our developers spend more time on solving interesting problems and less on repetitive tasks.

You will join a team of skilled developers who love what they do and, in a role, where you can have a big impact both on what is being built and how it is built. We value having our developers being part of refinement and you will be deeply involved in finding great solutions from a technical as well as a user perspective together with our Head of Products and UI/UX designers.

Required skills:

• 
3+ years of working with .NET and excellent C# programming skills

• 
Professional usage of an IDE like Visual Studio or Rider

• 
Work in an agile environment with a strong focus on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and clear communication

• 
Good understanding of architectural patterns and software design principles

• 
Good communication skills and a positive and proactive mindset

• 
Experience with Git and Azure Infrastructure

Additional skills (not required, but nice to have):

• 
Experience with using AI-assisted development tools (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude)

• 
Experience with Docker and Azure Pipelines

All we ask is that you bring passion, curiosity and structure to our workplace. We are a company of many nationalities. Whether you are from abroad or already living in Denmark, we welcome talented people of any gender, nationality and belief. We think the right mix of people makes for the best culture and product.

At Trackman, we see AI not as a replacement for great developers, but as a tool that makes great developers even more effective — accelerating code reviews, catching bugs earlier, and freeing up time for the creative problem-solving that moves our products forward.

The IT landscape is evolving faster than ever and staying up to date with AI-assisted development is quickly becoming a fundamental part of the software development process.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

Share our Passion!

Applications are continuously assessed, so please send your application as soon as possible.

At Bavarian Nordic, we are committed to saving and improving lives by unlocking the power of the immune system. Our commercial product portfolio includes market-leading vaccines against smallpox, mpox, rabies, tick-borne encephalitis, typhoid fever, and cholera.

We excel in R&D innovation, manufacturing, and commercialization, striving to improve people's health and quality of life worldwide, protecting our tomorrow.

We are seeking a Group Compliance Manager who will service as the center of compliance excellence and provide operational and administrative support across our Group Compliance programs.

The role will conduct risk-based third-party due diligence screenings and provide business-line advice to mitigate identified risks, conduct compliance training, support investigation case management, and support data privacy monitoring and follow-up.

About the team

You will join the Legal & Compliance team and work closely with Group Compliance program heads, Regional Legal & Compliance teams, corporate functions, and business stakeholders.

The position is located at our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, and reporting to the Head of Group Compliance Due Diligence Program.

About the role

As Group Compliance Manager, you will support the effective operation of key Group Compliance programs. You will conduct compliance due diligence screenings and provide business-line compliance advice, contribute to internal investigations, conduct compliance training and support the overall execution of training and communication priorities, and support data privacy documentation and reporting.

In this newly established role, you will help translate Group Compliance requirements into practical, well-documented processes and provide reliable support to stakeholders across functions and regions.

Key Responsibilities

• Administer due diligence systems and manage the intake, prioritization, status tracking, and records for third-party due diligence requests

• Independently conduct risk-based due diligence screenings, prepare screening reports, identify risk indicators, and recommend proportionate mitigating actions to the business

• Maintain screening documentation and prepare periodic management reports on anti-corruption, competition law, sanctions and export controls, and data privacy risks

• Support investigation case management, including intake, assignment, coordination, documentation, status tracking, remediation, closure, and reporting

• Contribute to the delivery of Group Compliance training, communications, and read-and-sign campaigns, including completion reporting

• Assist with the establishment and administration of data privacy management systems, templates, registers, assessments, agreements, gap records, and key compliance metrics

What you bring

At Bavarian Nordic, we are driven by purpose, accountability, and integrity. We are looking for a structured and hands-on compliance professional who can manage detailed workflows, conduct sound risk assessments, maintain accurate records, and collaborate effectively with stakeholders across the organization.

You likely bring:

• Master’s degree in law, finance/accounting, business, or a related field

• Minimum 3 years’ in-house corporate compliance experience

• Hands-on experience in due diligence, case management, and compliance training

• Regulated-industry experience is an advantage

You have a sharp eye for details and an analytical mindset. You understand the business and can communicate clearly and persuasively.

Why join Bavarian Nordic?

As we continue to develop our compliance function, you will help strengthen the day-to-day operation, documentation, monitoring, and reporting of our global programs.

In this role, you will:

• Work across key Group Compliance programs in a global, regulated business

• Gain hands-on experience in due diligence, investigations, training, communications, and data privacy

• Be part of a function grounded in professionalism, integrity, accountability, and collaboration

Alongside these opportunities, we offer:

• A collaborative workplace with colleagues across countries and functions

• Professional development opportunities and exposure to the wider business

• Flexible working conditions, pension, health insurance, and bonus opportunities

• A high-quality canteen with a wide selection and take-away options

• Fitness discounts, a massage scheme, and an active staff club offering social and sporting events

Salary

Annual base salary range: DKK 720,000 to 900,000 gross.

At Bavarian Nordic, we are committed to fair and transparent pay. The final base salary within this range will be determined based on the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, and competencies, as well as internal pay equity.

Interested?

If you are ready to bring your compliance expertise to a fast-growing global vaccine company, apply now and join Bavarian Nordic in our mission to improve health outcomes and foster sustainable growth.

Please note that for this position, we do not support any relocation packages. Candidates must possess a legal basis to work and reside in Denmark.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

Bavarian Nordic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

For more information, visit www.bavarian-nordic.com

**Join us to Make an Impact

**Innovation is in our DNA. We invented supercontinuum lasers and photonic crystal fibers and we constantly reimagine how our products can be used and improved. Our customers use our products in medical and life science research, quantum computing and space exploration.

We seek curious, creative and collaborative people to work in our cutting-edge company. Can you see yourself working in teams and providing solutions for innovators?

We are rapidly growing, so we are looking for an additional engineer to join our New Product Introduction (NPI) team.

Our NPI team is organized in Product Engineering within Engineering. NPI bridges the gap between product development and volume production, being the place where prototypes and first sales units are manufactured and tested.

NPI is working closely together with development engineers (optical, electrical, mechanical and software engineers) for maturing the product, but also with automation engineers on manufacturing processes.

When a product has proven it can be manufactured with satisfactory yield and volume justifies, it will be transferred to our Operations department, freeing up space and resources for the new next thing.

In NPI we have a team of highly skilled technicians and engineers. Our technicians are the crank as they are manufacturing by far the most prototypes and sales units.

As NPI Engineer you will:

• Mastering and improving existing production processes – training, and supporting technicians.

• Troubleshooting issues, performing failure analysis, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions.

• Analyzing test and manufacturing data to identify and implement improvements in quality and productivity.

• Collaborating with Operations and other departments to transfer mature products and processes into production.

**Qualifications

**To succeed in this role, you should have a technical background in one or more of the following areas: optics/photonics, electronics, or production engineering. You have a strong affinity for processes and enjoy enabling others to follow them accurately.

Additionally, you bring:

• Experience with complex technical systems (e.g., optical fibers, free space optics, or electronic test setups).

• A proactive and process-driven mindset.

• A few years of experience from a manufacturing environment.

• Proficiency in written and spoken English. Being able to speak Danish is an advantage, but not a requirement.

• You thrive in an environment where technical challenges and deadlines are part of everyday life. You enjoy teamwork – asking for help when needed and supporting colleagues when possible.

**Keep your personal data safe

**Hamamatsu ("The Company") take responsibly for the protection of your personal data. Accordingly, upon receiving your job application and additional material you choose to submit, the Company keeps a safe and secure environment and ensures confidentiality.

You also have a role to play in keeping your personal data safe. We request you only submit personal data about yourself in your job application, CV / Résumé or other relevant material you choose to provide to us that is relevant for the specific job opening you are applying for.

Please consider whether there is personal information you are about to submit, such as health information, information on family relations, information on trade union membership, etc. that is not necessary for our recruitment process or the job opening you are applying for. Please also be aware that certificates or other documents are not necessary for the vacancy. We urgently request you to redact/cross out such information before you submit your job application.

Thank you.

**Job Description

**

Data Platform Manager

Posting Start Date: 10/14/26

Gentofte, DNK, 2820,

**Data Platform Manager, Digital & IT

**

• Location: Lisbon, Portugal or Copenhagen, Denmark

• Working hours: Full-time

• Work model: Hybrid

• Contract type: Permanent

Are you passionate about building high-performing teams and shaping modern data platforms that enable business growth? Do you enjoy bringing together people, technology, and business needs to deliver scalable data solutions? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

As our new Data Platform Manager, you will be part of the Digital & IT organization and play an important role in advancing our enterprise data and analytics capabilities. You will lead a distributed team of data engineers while working closely with business stakeholders, Enterprise Architects, and technology teams across multiple locations to deliver reliable, secure, and scalable data solutions. This is a great opportunity to influence technology decisions, develop people, and shape the future of our data platform in an international organization.

**What Your Day Will Look Like

**In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Leading, coaching, and developing a team of data engineers across multiple locations, fostering a culture of collaboration, ownership, and continuous learning.

• Guiding the development, operation, and continuous improvement of a secure, scalable, and reliable cloud data platform.

• Establishing and promoting data engineering standards and best practices covering development, testing, deployment, monitoring, and documentation.

• Partnering with business stakeholders, Enterprise Architects, and technology teams to translate business requirements into practical and scalable data solutions.

• Overseeing the design and delivery of data pipelines, data models, and integrations from core business systems, including SAP, into the enterprise data platform.

• Shaping the platform roadmap by identifying opportunities to simplify, modernize, optimize costs, and create long-term business value.

**What You'll Bring

**

• Experience leading a data engineering, analytics engineering, or data platform team.

• Strong hands-on data engineering experience, including designing and building scalable, production-grade data pipelines and modern data warehouse or lakehouse solutions.

• Experience working with cloud data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, or Snowflake, combined with strong SQL and Python skills.

• Strong leadership, coaching, stakeholder management, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and business functions.

• Solid understanding of data engineering practices including ETL/ELT, data integration, CI/CD, data quality, operational monitoring, and DevOps principles.

• Experience working with SAP data environments, such as SAP S/4HANA, ECC, BW/BW4HANA, Datasphere, Business Data Cloud (BDC), or SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), would be considered an advantage.

**Working At STG & What To Expect

**At Scandinavian Tobacco Group (STG), we are so much more than what meets the eye. We combine the strength of global brands with the entrepreneurial mindset that allows people to make a real impact. Here you'll have the opportunity to grow your career, collaborate across borders, and help shape what's next.

Ready to be part of something bigger? Apply now and discover much more.

We assess each application against the key competencies and requirements for the role. If your experience and skills are a good match, you'll be invited to continue through our hiring process, which may include the following steps:

**Our Purpose

**Planday from Xero is a leading digital solution that uncomplicates everyday scheduling and workforce management by making it easier for businesses and shift workers around the world to communicate, collaborate, and get work done.

Powered by a community of local industry experts, Planday provides a best-in-class digital platform that is easy to use, accurate, secure, and compliant with local needs and standards. From payroll and accounting to POS and reporting, its open API and tech ecosystem is scalable to fit shifting business needs and to build an engaged, flexible workforce.

Founded in 2004, Planday is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark and supports over 400,000 users across Europe, Australia and the US. Planday was acquired by Xero in 2021.

**How You’ll Make An Impact

**As our Lead Engineer- Data, you will set the architectural direction of the data platform that enables both the decisions we make internally and the data-driven features our customers rely on. Working with the Data, ML, Platform, and Product Engineering teams, you will keep ingestion, modelling, and orchestration dependable, and define the modelling, testing, and documentation standards the data function depends on. You will innovate on how people work with data, building the agentic tooling and semantic modelling that let teams across Planday work from trusted data with confidence.

**What You’ll Do

**

• Set the architectural direction of our data platform so it serves analytics, product engineering, and AI/ML from one coherent design, collaborating with Platform and ML engineering on shared infrastructure.

• Design the dbt models, semantic layer, and quality standards the data function depends on, with the validation and lineage to make them trustworthy downstream.

• Own orchestration and observability in Dagster, and onboarding new sources in a way that scales.

• Innovate on self-serve and AI-enabled analytics, from semantic models and agentic workflows to our BI layer.

• Build the historical and low-latency foundations that make predictive and real-time use cases possible.

• Introduce better modelling standards, tooling, and development environments.

• Keep the platform reliable, performant, cost-effective, and compliant.

**Success looks like

**

• Architecture that holds up as we scale and as new use cases emerge, and that other engineers follow as a pattern.

• Analysts ship faster and more efficiently because your tooling & standards remove friction.

• A drop in repeat requests to the data team, as stakeholders answer their own questions through agentic workflows.

• ML and product teams have the historical and real-time data they need, without bespoke workarounds.

• Strong working relationships with the Data, ML, and Platform teams.

**What You’ll Bring With You

**

• Deep, hands-on Snowflake and dbt experience: modelling, semantic layers, agents & skills, testing, performance and cost tuning.

• Production experience with a pipeline orchestrator, ideally Dagster (or similar Airflow, Prefect), including dependent workloads, partial failures, and observability.

• Modern cloud infrastructure (Azure/AWS/GCP) and Kubernetes experience deploying and operating containerised workloads, plus infrastructure as code (Terraform).

• Strong SQL & Python for pipelines, services, and automation.

• Software engineering discipline across CI/CD, testing, and code review.

• The ability to turn technical trade-offs into clear narratives that help stakeholders decide and trust the work.

• Experience operating data systems, including incident response, cost, and data privacy practices.

**At Planday, we offer you

**

• Benefits like pension, health insurance, inclusive support for new parents and generous vacation

• On top of your annual base salary, you are offered to be part of an Employee Share Plan

• Growth and progression opportunities – we want you to grow with us

• Flexible remote work

• Strong social culture with lots of team and company activities

• Meaningful work – everyone at Planday contributes to improving the lives of shift workers around the globe

• Healthy work-life balance and autonomous approach to work. We trust in you and your abilities

Finally, our offices are not just workplaces (although they are pretty nice and well-located, we have to say!). Plandayers are open and welcoming and at Planday, everyone has the freedom and support to show their true self at work.

_At Planday, we firmly believe that diversity and inclusion are the cornerstones of innovation and a vibrant workplace culture. As an equal opportunity employer, we strive to create an equitable experience for all candidates throughout the process. As Safety Surveillance Principal Process Specialist, you will keep Safety Surveillance ready for every audit and inspection, and make sure the way we monitor safety information keeps pace with legislation. You will be a highly visible process expert: leading our contribution to inspections, co-driving regulatory surveillance and shaping how we integrate processes after acquisitions. Your work keeps surveillance of Novo’s marketed and developmental products compliant, simpler and focused on the work that adds most value.

What you’ll bring

You know drug safety from the inside, and you know what it takes to get an organisation ready for an inspection. You will also bring:

• A Master’s degree in Life Sciences, such as Pharmacy, Medicine, Veterinary Science or Biology, or a related field.

• At least 5–7 years of experience in pharmacovigilance, including supporting safety activities in clinical trials.

• Hands-on experience facilitating inspection set-ups, training colleagues and preparing an organisation for audits and inspections.

• Expertise in Safety Surveillance processes and an enterprise mindset: you understand the end-to-end process and can turn complex internal and external requirements into practical ways of working.

• A solid background in handling deviations and implementing process changes.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage and influence senior internal stakeholders and external parties, and a collaborative mindset across functions and geographies.

• Resilience and a calm demeanour in a very busy environment, with the ability to multitask and prioritise your workload through complexity and challenge.

Desirable, but not essential:

Experience in process management and project management.

What you’ll do

You will be a recognised expert in key Safety Surveillance processes, helping the team work with greater simplicity and focus. The role covers a diverse range of tasks, and you could be part of an inspection from day one.

• Lead audits and inspections: coordinate Safety Surveillance contributions, prepare colleagues for interviews, ensure high-quality responses and keep oversight of findings and the associated corrective and preventive actions.

• Act as Process Expert for the signal management process and co-drive the Regulatory Surveillance process, ensuring full compliance with applicable legislation.

• Handle deviations and change requests in close collaboration with colleagues in Safety Surveillance and other relevant functions.

• Support integration and acquisition activities by helping integrate pharmacovigilance processes and systems following company or product acquisitions and mergers.

• Contribute to process improvement projects aligned with our strategic objectives, using your end-to-end view of Safety Surveillance.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Safety Surveillance Centre of Expertise, a team of five engaged and skilled colleagues within Safety Surveillance, and report to the Director of Safety Surveillance Centre of Expertise.

Safety Surveillance is a department within Global Patient Safety in Research & Development, with departments in Bangalore, India, and Boston, US. Together, we are globally accountable for surveillance of all safety information for Novo’s marketed products and products in development. We also handle safety label updates, Risk Management Plans and aggregate reports.

You will work closely with colleagues across Safety Surveillance and partner with Global Patient Safety, other headquarters functions and affiliates during audits and inspections. When processes need to change, you will bring the right people together, create clarity on what needs to happen and help the team move forward with pace.

What you can expect here

You will have real visibility as a process expert, and the opportunity to influence how Safety Surveillance works and make a lasting impact. You will be trusted to take ownership, encouraged to make your voice heard, and supported by colleagues who give honest feedback and never compromise on patient safety or quality.

The pace is high and the work is varied. Through process improvement projects and a broad range of tasks, you will build new skills and deepen your understanding of safety surveillance end to end.

jobs.description:
With more than 8,000 employees, Deloitte is one of the largest professional services firms across the Nordics. We help clients navigate complex business and technology transformations by combining deep industry expertise with leading capabilities in Audit, Tax, Advisory, and Consulting.

About the team

Join our Transfer Pricing team of more than 45 colleagues in Copenhagen and Aarhus. We help international and Danish businesses turn complex tax, finance and operating-model questions into practical solutions. As a Manager, you will bring your experience to a collaborative team, take a leading role in client engagements and contribute to developing our people and practice.

You will lead a broad range of projects for clients across sectors. Working with colleagues across Deloitte, you will turn complex analyses into practical advice and take responsibility for engagements from planning through to delivery. You will also help develop less experienced colleagues and continue building your own technical and leadership skills through training in Denmark and at Deloitte University in Paris.

Ready to take the next step in your career? In this role, you will:

• Manage transfer pricing engagements across advisory, compliance and disputes, overseeing teams, timelines and quality.

• Build client relationships and deliver practical advice with colleagues across Deloitte’s international network.

• Develop less experienced colleagues through feedback, work review and knowledge sharing.

• Help grow our practice by spotting new opportunities and shaping solutions for existing and new clients.

We work in a dynamic, international environment with an informal tone, where quality, collaboration and different perspectives are central to how we create value for clients and for each other.

AI-enabled and digital tools are a natural part of how we work. You will help identify where they can add value to research, analysis and delivery, while applying sound judgement and maintaining responsibility for the quality of the work. No specialist AI expertise is required, but curiosity and a willingness to improve how we work matter most.

We value the community that extends beyond client work. Our employee association brings people together throughout the year - from social events to shared experiences that cut across teams and business units. We celebrate the wins, big and small, and make a point of recognising individual and shared milestones.

The role is full-time, and we are looking for professionals for our offices in both Copenhagen and Aarhus, Denmark.

We are looking for experienced transfer pricing professionals who are ready to take responsibility for client engagements and contribute to the development of our team. You may already be working as a Manager ready for the next step.

You combine technical expertise with a practical understanding of client needs. You take ownership, collaborate openly and are comfortable coordinating the work of others while remaining hands-on with analysis and delivery.

What you bring to the team:

• A relevant academic background, such as law, economics, finance, accounting or business.

• Solid experience in transfer pricing, gained in an advisory firm, an in-house role or a comparable environment (minimum 5 years).

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn complex technical and financial information into clear recommendations.

• Curiosity about technology and judgement when using AI-enabled tools.

• Clear written and verbal communication, and confidence discussing technical matters with clients and colleagues.

• An interest in developing others through guidance, feedback and knowledge sharing.

• A strong client-service mindset and an interest in building relationships and contributing to new opportunities.

• Work permit in Denmark

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Do you want to be part of our team?

Team Leadership & Development

Over one million Danes use Skatteguiden to understand and optimise their taxes. We automate tax tracking, surface deductions people didn't know they had, and give users the insight they need to make better financial decisions. All connected directly to the Danish tax authority. We're an independent company of around 50 people based in Copenhagen, with a 4.7-star rating and a simple mission: make financial insight accessible to everyone, not just those who can afford an accountant.

Our platform has grown with us. The infrastructure that keeps Skatteguiden running has reached a scale and complexity that deserves full-time, specialist ownership, and the work ahead makes this an unusually good time to join.

About the role

You'll be joining the Platform team as a Platform Application Engineer, the counterpart to our Operational Platform team, which owns the infrastructure. Where they own the systems that keep Skatteguiden running, you'll own the shared application-layer services that the rest of engineering depends on.

The team treats these services as a product, with engineers distributed across several product teams as their users. Every product team touches payments, identity, and integrations. Your job is to make those services reliable, well-designed, and genuinely easy to build on, across a microservices architecture that favours low coupling and event-driven communication over direct dependencies.

We operate on a simple principle: you build it, you own it. That means end-to-end accountability, from design and implementation through to what happens when something goes wrong. Incidents aren't escalated to someone else's queue; they're yours to understand, resolve, and learn from.

What you'll do

Own the shared application platform. Design and build the core backend services underpinning payments, identity, authorisation, and third-party integrations — the shared foundation that product teams rely on every day.

Build and maintain payment services. Design payment flows that are reliable, observable, and compliant. Work with product teams to support new features and providers without coupling concerns or creating fragility in the critical path.

Own identity and authorisation. Design the systems that manage who our users are and what they can do — from OAuth flows and token management to fine-grained permission models and audit trails.

Integrate security and privacy into the application layer. Work with our Head of Security & Privacy to translate requirements into technical controls — particularly in identity, authorisation, and data handling — with GDPR and ISO 27001 in mind.

Integrate third-party systems. Own the integration layer connecting messaging, payment providers, and others. Ensure resilience, observability, and clear contracts.

Improve the developer experience. Build shared libraries, abstractions, and internal tooling that make it easier for product engineers to build on top of platform services correctly and confidently. Reduce the cognitive load on teams that shouldn't need to think about auth or payment internals.

Who we're looking for

You're likely a senior backend or platform engineer who's built and operated shared application services at scale, and who sees that role not just as backend development but as a product discipline — with the engineers who depend on your services as your primary users.

You take end-to-end ownership seriously. You don't consider something done when the code is merged, you care about how it behaves in production, you're on the hook when it doesn't, and you treat incidents as feedback worth acting on.

You're genuinely collaborative, someone who makes the people around them better, shares context freely, and doesn't work in isolation. And you're curious: you like trying new things, you're not attached to the way things have always been done, and you get energy from learning.

Must-have

A senior backend or platform engineer who's built and operated shared application services at scale, writes clean, maintainable services, takes API design seriously, and cares about the boundaries between components.

Hands-on experience deploying and debugging services on Kubernetes in production; you know how to get code running reliably in a Kubernetes environment without needing to own the cluster.

Experience designing MySQL schemas for production, migrations, indexing, query performance, and keeping data models clean as requirements evolve.

Working knowledge of message brokers such as RabbitMQ, event-driven patterns, consumer reliability, and how to design async communication that is easy to reason about across a distributed codebase.

Understanding of identity and authorisation (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT, RBAC), and how to implement them securely and maintainably at scale.

Security, privacy, and compliance awareness. You design with GDPR, auditability, and least-privilege access in mind from the start, not as an afterthought.

A platform as a product mindset. Experience thinking about developer experience as a product discipline, not just an engineering concern.

Genuine enthusiasm for AI. You use it daily, and you're always looking for new ways to apply it.

Nice-to-have

Experience building or operating payment integrations — familiarity with PSPs, webhook reliability, idempotency, and reconciliation.

Familiarity with React and TypeScript — enough to read, understand, and occasionally contribute to frontend code when the work calls for it.

Familiarity with Azure. You know your way around the platform — how services connect, how access and permissions work, and how to build in a cloud-native context.

Familiarity with our observability stack: Prometheus, Grafana, Sentry.

Familiarity with our GitOps tooling: ArgoCD and GitHub Actions.

Why join us

A substantial project from day one. The hosting migration means designing a production system from scratch, rare at any company.

Real influence. The architectural decisions made in this team will shape how Skatteguiden is built and operated for years. It's a small team with a high degree of autonomy, and the work is genuinely consequential.

Strong engineering culture. We take the technical foundations seriously. Security, architecture, and technical debt get real attention, not just lip service.

The product matters. Over one million Danes use Skatteguiden. Your work keeps it running and makes it possible to grow.

Solid company. We're independent, profitable, and growing. No VC pressure, no bloated roadmap. Just a clear mission and a team that cares.

A company that's serious about AI. We use AI across the business and we're only going deeper. Being a small, focused team means we can move fast on this, no lengthy approval chains, no slow rollouts. If you're always looking for ways to work smarter with AI, you'll fit right in.

Good people. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. The culture is professional, informal, and genuinely collaborative.

Practical detailsLocation

Copenhagen. We're an office-first company, and it's a deliberate choice. We're moving fast, we have big ambitions, and we genuinely believe that being physically together is one of the things that makes that possible. Things move quicker when you can turn your chair and talk to someone. We want to be upfront about this so you know what to expect.

And if we're asking people to be in the office, we want it to be worth their while. We're a five-minute walk from Rådhuspladsen, stocked with everything from fruit to fizzy drinks to afternoon snacks, and lunch is at Claus Meyer's canteen just across the street, proper food, not an afterthought. If you're putting in a long day, dinner is covered too.

Start: As soon as possible

Salary: Competitive and based on your experience.

Reporting to: CTO

Screening call with our recruiter (30 min) ONLINE

Technical interview with the manager and an engineer (120 min) ONSITE

Meeting with our CEO (45 min) ONSITE
